> Written with Claude Code.

## Motivation

HiCache's `direct` IO backend moves `page_first_direct` pages with the copy engine. Before each transfer it syncs the token-slot indices to the CPU and builds one copy descriptor per (page, layer). For an MLA model with a DSA indexer (GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-V3.2) that host-side work dominates each transfer: about 0.5 us of CPU issue per page and layer, paid on every load-back and write-back.

## Modifications

The PR has two commits; reviewing them separately is easiest.

1. **`[Refactor] kvcache: Move the page_row op out of nvfp4_hicache`** moves the page-row transfer op (`_jit_page_row_module`, `warmup_page_row_transfer`, `transfer_page_rows`) unchanged from `ops/kvcache/nvfp4_hicache.py` to `ops/kvcache/page_row.py`, so host pools other than MiniMax NVFP4 can use it. No behavior change; the diff is large but contains no edits.
2. **`[Feat] hicache: Add a direct_kernel IO backend ...`** adds `--hicache-io-backend direct_kernel` for the same `page_first_direct` layout. It copies with `page_row.cuh` SM kernels that read the token-slot indices on the GPU and access the pinned host pool in place, so nothing syncs to the CPU and no descriptors are built:
   - `page_row` gains a token-slot index stride (page `p` is `indices[p * stride] / stride`), a runtime CTA quota (0 sizes the grid to the work; MiniMax NVFP4 keeps its default), and probes for a coherent host link and for GPU access to registered host memory at its CPU virtual address. Stride 1 launches its own kernel instantiation without the stride arithmetic, so MiniMax NVFP4's page-id copies keep their device code.
   - `MLATokenToKVPoolHost` and `DSAIndexerPoolHost` validate the backend and build their pointer tables in a new `prepare_io_backend`, which the controller calls at startup for every pool in the host group. `HybridCacheController.register_host_pool_entry` calls it for a sidecar that registers later (a draft pool not packed into the target pools, e.g. EAGLE3 on an MLA/DSA model). Every other host pool, DeepSeek-V4's `LogicalHostPool` included, rejects the backend at startup.
   - Startup fails with the cause when a page is not a multiple of 128 bytes, the kernels fail to load, or the GPU cannot use registered host memory at its CPU virtual address (`cudaDevAttrCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem`).
   - Write-back moves all layers of a pool in one launch; load moves one layer per launch, so layer-wise load overlap is unchanged.
   - The server-arg hook requires (or resolves to) `page_first_direct`, and names `--disaggregation-decode-host-receive-threshold` when that option forced `layer_first`.
   - On a pre-Blackwell GPU with a non-coherent (PCIe) host link it logs a warning, since SM stores to host memory there are expected to lose to the copy engine.
   - Docs: `hicache_design.mdx` and `server_arguments.mdx` describe the new choice and its limits.

`direct` and `kernel` are unchanged; `direct_kernel` is opt-in.

## Accuracy Tests

`nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` on one 4x GB300 node: TP4, EAGLE MTP 3-1-4, HiCache `write_back` on `page_first_direct` with a 120 GB host pool per rank. Three servers differ only in the cache flags: radix cache only, `--hicache-io-backend direct`, `--hicache-io-backend direct_kernel`. The device KV pool is capped at 131,072 tokens (`--max-total-tokens`) so that repeated prompts are evicted to the host pool and reloaded from it. Other differences from the cookbook's GB300 NVFP4 low-latency recipe: MTP 3-1-4 instead of 5-1-6, `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE and FP4 GEMM with `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`, `--max-running-requests 64`.

**Long-document key retrieval through the host pool.** 96 synthetic documents of ~18k tokens, each hiding 8 seven-digit codes at depths from 4% to 96% of high-entropy filler. Pass 1 asks for one code per document; the documents total 1.76M tokens, 13x the device pool. Pass 2 resends every document and asks for all 8 codes, so its prefix is reloaded from the host pool (HiCache arms) or recomputed (radix only). Greedy decoding, thinking off; the cache source of each request comes from `return_cached_tokens_details`.

| | radix only | `direct` | `direct_kernel` |
|---|---|---|---|
| pass 1 (96 codes) | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| pass 2 (768 codes) | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| pass 2 prompt tokens served from host | 0 | 99.3% (1,756,864 of 1,768,695) | 99.3% (1,756,864 of 1,768,695) |
| MTP accept length, whole run (of 4) | 3.54 | 3.48 | 3.49 |

The MTP draft layer's KV is packed into the same host pool and reloaded with it; an intact target with a corrupted draft would keep the answers right but drop the accept length, which stays level.

**GSM8K**, `sgl-eval` 0.1.2, all 1,319 problems, temperature 0, `enable_thinking=false`, `--max-tokens 4096`, 64 threads, run twice per server. In run 2, 68% of the prompt tokens were reloaded from the host pool on both HiCache arms.

| | radix only | `direct` | `direct_kernel` |
|---|---|---|---|
| run 1 | 84.15% | 84.99% | 83.93% |
| run 2 (reloaded from host) | 84.84% | 84.23% | 84.91% |

All six scores lie within 1.1 pp of each other (one standard error is about 1.0 pp at n = 1,319). Thinking is off and sampling greedy, rather than the recommended temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 with thinking, to keep the runs short and comparable, so the absolute scores sit below the model's thinking-mode GSM8K. No request errors, tracebacks or NaNs on any server.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`test/manual/kernels/bench_hicache_direct.py` (new) on one GB300 (NVLink-C2C host link), GLM-5.2 per-rank shape under DP attention (78 MLA layers, 21 DSA indexer layers). One serialized radix-node step: evict (D2H) then load (H2D), wall time including index moves and the completion sync:

| pages/step | load `direct` -> `direct_kernel` | write-back `direct` -> `direct_kernel` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2.91 -> 1.41 ms | 0.28 -> 0.14 ms |
| 64 | 7.04 -> 1.58 ms | 2.78 -> 1.13 ms |
| 1024 | 35.1 -> 15.5 ms | 34.4 -> 16.3 ms |

On a B300 host with a PCIe host link, `direct_kernel` matched `direct` on large loads and beat it on write-back (52 vs 40 GB/s at 1024 pages) and on small loads.

MiniMax NVFP4 also copies through `page_row` (`--hicache-io-backend kernel`, its default), so its transfers were measured with and without this PR on one GB300: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash host pools, 60 layers, the main KV row at TP4 / TP2 / attention-TP1 (18 / 36 / 72 KiB per page) and the indexer row (9 KiB per page), 1-512 pages, load as one launch per layer and write-back as one launch for all layers, median of 3 runs.

| pages | write-back, all rows | load, all rows |
|---|---|---|
| 1-8 | -3.3% to +0.6% | -1.9% to +4.2% (bound by host launch time, ~0.4 ms for 60 launches) |
| 64-512 | -0.2% to +0.1% | -1.5% to -0.2% |

The one cost is host launch time: the two added launch arguments add 0.1-0.25 us per launch (of ~6.3 us), which shows only in the smallest loads.

In serving, the accuracy servers above report the same effect through their own timers (`sglang:load_back_duration_seconds` and `sglang:hicache_backup_duration_seconds`, the GPU-stream span of each copy loop). Per rank, as the range over the 4 TP ranks:

| phase | volume per rank | `direct` | `direct_kernel` |
|---|---|---|---|
| long-document pass 2, load-back | 85 GB in 51-54 merged loads | 1.44-1.47 s | 0.55-0.57 s |
| long-document run, write-back | 86 GB in ~483 backups | 1.31-1.34 s | 0.50 s |
| GSM8K run 2, load-back | 3.8 GB in 583 loads | 2.54-2.78 s | 0.63-0.78 s |
| GSM8K run 2, write-back | 9.9 GB in ~1,190 backups | 0.39-0.40 s | 0.10 s |

End-to-end request latencies of these short runs are not a useful comparison: both servers started cold, and serving-time Triton compilations (3-4.5 s each, at different moments on each server) dominate the pass times.

A 30-minute agentic-coding replay of GLM-5.2-NVFP4 (3 prefill workers at PP4 with HiCache `write_back` + `direct_kernel`, 1 decode worker at DEP8, MTP; 20 GB300 GPUs) served 16,989 requests with 0 errors on this branch's transfer path before its rebase onto current main.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Tests (all pass on GB300):
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hicache_direct.py`: page_row-backed transfers are bit-exact against the source pages.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsa_pool_host_unit.py`: the GLM-5.2 MLA + indexer pair prepared through `HostPoolGroup`, `direct_kernel` byte-identical to `direct`, with a packed MTP layer.

+"""Page-granular HiCache transfers for the ``page_first_direct`` host layout.
+
+These back ``--hicache-io-backend direct_kernel``: page-row copies
+(``kvcacheio/page_row.cuh``) that read the transfer indices on the GPU and access
+the pinned host pool in place. The ``direct`` backend instead syncs the indices to
+the CPU and builds copy-engine descriptors there, submitted as one
+cudaMemcpyBatchAsync when the runtime has it and as per-page copies otherwise.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from typing import NamedTuple, Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import cache_once, is_hip_runtime
+from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.page_row import (
+    page_row_host_link_coherent,
+    page_row_host_pointer_usable,
+    transfer_page_rows,
+    warmup_page_row_transfer,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class HiCacheDirectTables(NamedTuple):
+    """Page-row pointer tables for one page_first_direct host pool.
+
+    ``host[l]`` is the mapped address of host layer ``l`` in host page 0 and
+    ``device[l]`` the base of the device layer stored as host layer ``l``; both are
+    uint64 CUDA ``[num_layers]``. A page is ``row_bytes`` on both sides; host pages
+    are ``host_stride`` apart.
+    """
+
+    host: torch.Tensor
+    device: torch.Tensor
+    host_stride: int
+    row_bytes: int
+
+    def split_layers(self) -> tuple[HiCacheDirectTables, ...]:
+        """One single-layer table per host layer; build once, slicing per call is
+        a measurable share of a small transfer."""
+        return tuple(
+            self._replace(host=self.host[i : i + 1], device=self.device[i : i + 1])
+            for i in range(self.host.numel())
+        )
+
+
+def make_hicache_direct_tables(
+    host_pool: torch.Tensor, device_layer_ptrs: torch.Tensor
+) -> HiCacheDirectTables:
+    """Tables for a contiguous ``[host_page, num_layers, ...]`` host pool whose
+    device layers are ``device_layer_ptrs`` (uint64 CUDA, host layer order)."""
+    num_layers = host_pool.shape[1]
+    row_bytes = host_pool[0, 0].nbytes
+    assert host_pool.is_contiguous() and device_layer_ptrs.numel() == num_layers
+    base = host_pool.data_ptr()
+    host = torch.tensor(
+        [base + layer * row_bytes for layer in range(num_layers)],
+        dtype=torch.uint64,
+        device=device_layer_ptrs.device,
+    )
+    return HiCacheDirectTables(
+        host, device_layer_ptrs, num_layers * row_bytes, row_bytes
+    )
+
+
+def hicache_direct_kernel_unavailable_reason(*, page_bytes: int) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Why `page_bytes`-byte pages cannot use these transfers, or None if they can.
+

+    first transfer.
+    """

+        return "it is CUDA-only"
+    if page_bytes <= 0 or page_bytes % 128 != 0:

+        f"HiCache direct_kernel on GPU {device_id}: SM copies to host memory over "

+        "consider --hicache-io-backend direct."

+"""Opaque page-row transfers between pinned host memory and paged device pools."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import (
+    cache_once,
+    is_hip_runtime,
+    load_jit,
+    make_cpp_args,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from tvm_ffi.module import Module
+
+# Sixteen 16 B loads in flight per lane measured fastest on B300 PCIe for MSA
+# rows: ~51 GB/s H2D and ~52 GB/s D2H, vs 46 / 35 GB/s with 8 / 32 per lane.
+_VECS_PER_LANE = 16
+_BLOCK_SIZE = 512
+# Two CTAs saturate B300 PCIe; MI350X needs 16 or more (measured on gfx950).
+_DEFAULT_BLOCK_QUOTA = 32 if is_hip_runtime() else 2
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _jit_page_row_module(*, load: bool) -> Module:
+    args = make_cpp_args(load, _VECS_PER_LANE, _BLOCK_SIZE)
+    return load_jit(
+        "page_row",
+        *args,
+        cuda_files=["kvcacheio/page_row.cuh"],
+        cuda_wrappers=[
+            ("run", f"&PageRowKernel<{args}>::run"),
+            ("host_link_coherent", "&page_row_host_link_coherent"),
+            ("host_pointer_usable", "&page_row_host_pointer_usable"),
+        ],
+    )
+
+
+def warmup_page_row_transfer() -> None:
+    """Compile both directions before requests can submit transfers, so compile
+    errors surface at pool construction rather than mid-serving."""
+    _jit_page_row_module(load=True)
+    _jit_page_row_module(load=False)
+
+
+def page_row_host_link_coherent(device_id: int) -> bool:
+    """Whether the GPU reaches pageable host memory through the host page tables,
+    as on a coherent NVLink-C2C link."""
+    return bool(_jit_page_row_module(load=True).host_link_coherent(device_id))
+
+
+def page_row_host_pointer_usable(device_id: int) -> bool:
+    """Whether kernels may use the host address of cudaHostRegister-ed memory
+    (host pointer tables hold host addresses)."""
+    return bool(_jit_page_row_module(load=True).host_pointer_usable(device_id))
+
+
+def transfer_page_rows(
+    host_ptrs: torch.Tensor,
+    device_ptrs: torch.Tensor,
+    host_pages: torch.Tensor,
+    device_pages: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    host_stride: int,
+    device_stride: int,
+    row_bytes: int,
+    load: bool,
+    index_stride: int = 1,
+    block_quota: int = _DEFAULT_BLOCK_QUOTA,
+) -> None:
+    """Copy ``row_bytes`` per (layer, page) on the current stream.
+
+    ``host_ptrs`` / ``device_ptrs`` are CUDA uint64 ``[layers]`` row-0 addresses
+    (host addresses are mapped pinned memory); page ``p`` of a layer starts at
+    ``ptr + p * stride``. ``host_pages`` / ``device_pages`` are validated,
+    same-device CUDA int32/int64 indices whose page ``i`` is
+    ``pages[i * index_stride] // index_stride``: 1 for page ids, the page size for
+    page-aligned token slots. ``block_quota`` caps the grid; 0 sizes it to the work.
+    Bases, strides and ``row_bytes`` must be 128-byte aligned. The caller owns
+    buffers and indices until its stream completion event fires.
+    """

+        return

+        host_ptrs,
+        device_ptrs,
+        host_pages,
+        device_pages,
+        host_stride,
+        device_stride,
+        row_bytes,
+        index_stride,
+        block_quota,
+    )

+"""HiCache L2 transfers on GLM-5.2 shapes, as a chain of serialised radix-node steps.
+
+Under ``--hicache-write-policy write_back`` with serialised load-back, each radix
+node is loaded on its own: evict (a synchronous D2H write-back), then load (a
+synchronous H2D), then the next node, with no forward in flight. This times K such
+steps per node size through the submission path the controller uses: index moves,
+then ``L2TransferEngine`` (or the raw op for the all-layer load the engine does not
+offer), then the completion-event sync.
+
+Cases per node size P (pages per step):
+  cold   H2D only, distinct host pages per step, device L2 flushed before each step
+  warm   H2D only, the same pages every step, no flush
+  evict  D2H of P pages, then H2D of P pages, per step (cold)
+
+Arms:
+  direct              copy engine over page_first_direct
+  direct_kernel       page-row kernels through the host pools, one launch per layer
+  direct_kernel_all(raw)  the same kernels loading every layer in one launch per
+                      pool, as raw ops (no L2TransferEngine, no per-submission events)
+  kernel/q<n>         page_first TMA load + staged write-back, n CTAs
+
+Host indices are pageable or pinned (``--pin``), since a non_blocking upload of
+pageable indices may block the submitting thread.
+
+    python test/manual/kernels/bench_hicache_direct.py --layers 20 78 --check
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import ctypes
+import json
+import platform
+import statistics
+import subprocess
+import time
+from typing import Callable, NamedTuple
+
+import torch
+
+import sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.hicache as hicache_ops
+from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.hicache_direct import (
+    make_hicache_direct_tables,
+    transfer_hicache_direct,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.page_row import page_row_host_link_coherent
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hybrid_cache.host_pool_config import (
+    prepare_host_pool_config,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.l2_transfer import L2Transfer, L2TransferEngine
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import DSATokenToKVPool
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host.dsa import DSAIndexerPoolHost
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host.mla import MLATokenToKVPoolHost
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+
+PAGE_SIZE = 64
+KV_ROW_BYTES = PAGE_SIZE * 576
+INDEXER_ROW_BYTES = PAGE_SIZE * 132
+# GLM-5.2 (index_topk_freq 4): 7 indexer layers on the first 20-layer PP4 stage,
+# 21 of 78 on a DEP rank.
+GLM52_INDEXER_LAYERS = {20: 7, 78: 21}
+
+
+class Pools(NamedTuple):
+    target: DSATokenToKVPool
+    kv: MLATokenToKVPoolHost
+    indexer: DSAIndexerPoolHost
+
+    def destroy(self):
+        self.kv.destroy()
+        self.indexer.destroy()
+
+    def transfers(self, h, d) -> list[L2Transfer]:
+        # The indexer owns a subset of layers; it skips the rest itself.
+        return [
+            L2Transfer(self.kv, self.target, h, d),
+            L2Transfer(
+                self.indexer, self.target, h, d, layer_mapper=lambda layer: layer
+            ),
+        ]
+
+
+def _build(layers, indexer_layers, device_tokens, host_tokens, layout) -> Pools:
+    # Spread the indexer layers evenly, as shared-topk models interleave them.
+    owned = {round(i * layers / indexer_layers) for i in range(indexer_layers)}
+    target = DSATokenToKVPool(
+        size=device_tokens,
+        page_size=PAGE_SIZE,
+        kv_lora_rank=512,
+        dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn,
+        qk_rope_head_dim=64,
+        layer_num=layers,
+        device="cuda",
+        enable_memory_saver=False,
+        kv_cache_dim=576,
+        index_head_dim=128,
+        skip_topk_layers=[i not in owned for i in range(layers)],
+    )
+    kv_host = MLATokenToKVPoolHost(
+        buffer_info=target.get_device_pool_infos()[0].buffer_info,
+        host_to_device_ratio=host_tokens / device_tokens,
+        host_size=0,
+        page_size=PAGE_SIZE,
+        layout=layout,
+        pin_memory=True,
+        device="cpu",
+        override_kv_cache_dim=target.kv_cache_dim,
+        device_capacity_tokens=target.size,
+        start_layer=target.start_layer,
+        end_layer=target.end_layer,
+        target_layer_num=target.layer_num,
+    )
+    indexer_config = prepare_host_pool_config(
+        root=target,
+        full_layer_mapping={i: i for i in range(target.layer_num)},
+        transfer_layer_id_max=target.layer_num,
+        transfer_page_size=kv_host.page_size,
+    ).sidecars[0]
+    indexer_host = DSAIndexerPoolHost(
+        indexer_config.buffer_info,
+        layer_mapping=indexer_config.device_to_host_layer,
+        target_device_layer_num=target.layer_num,
+        num_host_pages=kv_host.page_num,
+        transfer_page_size=kv_host.page_size,
+        layout=kv_host.layout,
+        buffer_device=target.device,
+        dtype=target.store_dtype,
+        layer_sharded=target.layer_shard_enabled,
+    )
+    return Pools(target, kv_host, indexer_host)
+
+
+class Step(NamedTuple):
+    """One synchronous transfer: wall and submit time on the CPU, GPU time between events."""
+
+    wall_ms: float
+    submit_ms: float
+    gpu_ms: float
+
+
+class Arm(NamedTuple):
+    name: str
+    write_back: Callable[[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], Step]
+    load: Callable[[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], Step]
+
+
+def _upload(host_indices):
+    """HiCacheController.move_indices for the GPU-index backends."""
+    return host_indices.to("cuda", non_blocking=True)
+
+
+def _engine_arm(pools: Pools, backend: str, name: str, staged_write_cpu=False) -> Arm:
+    engine = L2TransferEngine(backend)
+    layers = pools.target.layer_num
+
+    def move(h, d):
+        if backend == "direct":
+            return h, d.cpu()
+        return _upload(h), d
+
+    def finish(t0, t1, completion):
+        completion.finish_event.synchronize()
+        t2 = time.perf_counter()
+        gpu = completion.start_event.elapsed_time(completion.finish_event)
+        return Step((t2 - t0) * 1e3, (t1 - t0) * 1e3, gpu)
+
+    def write_back(h, d):
+        t0 = time.perf_counter()
+        # HiCacheController._move_write_operation keeps CPU host indices for the
+        # staged page_first write-back.
+        h2, d2 = (h, d) if staged_write_cpu else move(h, d)
+        completion = engine.submit_device_to_host(pools.transfers(h2, d2))
+        return finish(t0, time.perf_counter(), completion)
+
+    # Preallocated and recorded once, as LayerLoadingEvent reuses its event sets:
+    # an event's first record() initialises it, which would bill the per-layer path.
+    start = torch.cuda.Event()
+    events = [torch.cuda.Event() for _ in range(layers)]
+    for event in (start, *events):
+        event.record()
+
+    def load(h, d):
+        t0 = time.perf_counter()
+        h2, d2 = move(h, d)
+        start.record()
+        completion = engine.submit_host_to_device(
+            pools.transfers(h2, d2),
+            transfer_layer_id_max=layers,
+            start_event=start,
+            on_layer_done=lambda layer: events[layer].record(),
+        )
+        return finish(t0, time.perf_counter(), completion)
+
+    return Arm(name, write_back, load)
+
+
+def _all_layer_arm(pools: Pools) -> Arm:
+    """direct_kernel with one launch per pool in both directions, around the raw op
+    with the controller's index move and stream discipline."""
+    tables = [
+        make_hicache_direct_tables(pools.kv.kv_buffer, pools.kv.device_data_ptrs),
+        make_hicache_direct_tables(
+            pools.indexer.index_k_with_scale_buffer, pools.indexer.index_k_device_ptrs
+        ),
+    ]
+    d2h, h2d = torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()
+    start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    start.record()
+    end.record()
+
+    def timed(stream, h, d, load):
+        t0 = time.perf_counter()
+        hg = _upload(h)
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            start.record()
+            for t in tables:
+                transfer_hicache_direct(t, hg, d, page_size=PAGE_SIZE, load=load)
+            end.record()
+        t1 = time.perf_counter()
+        end.synchronize()
+        t2 = time.perf_counter()
+        return Step((t2 - t0) * 1e3, (t1 - t0) * 1e3, start.elapsed_time(end))
+
+    return Arm(
+        "direct_kernel_all(raw)",
+        lambda h, d: timed(d2h, h, d, False),
+        lambda h, d: timed(h2d, h, d, True),
+    )
+
+
+def _token_indices(pages: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return (pages[:, None] * PAGE_SIZE + torch.arange(PAGE_SIZE)).reshape(-1)
+
+
+def _check(arm: Arm, pools: Pools, host_pages, device_pages, gen):
+    """Byte-exact round trip through a page_first_direct arm."""
+    dp = device_pages.cuda()
+    kv_layers = pools.kv.layer_num
+    idx_layers = pools.indexer.index_k_device_ptrs.numel()
+    host_rows = (
+        pools.kv.kv_buffer.view(torch.uint8).view(-1, kv_layers, KV_ROW_BYTES),
+        pools.indexer.index_k_with_scale_buffer.view(torch.uint8).view(
+            -1, idx_layers, INDEXER_ROW_BYTES
+        ),
+    )
+    device_rows = (
+        [
+            b.view(torch.uint8).view(-1, KV_ROW_BYTES)
+            for b in pools.kv.device_kv_buffers
+        ],
+        [
+            b.view(torch.uint8).view(-1, INDEXER_ROW_BYTES)
+            for b in pools.indexer.packed_device_index_buffers
+        ],
+    )
+    for rows in device_rows:
+        for r in rows:
+            r[dp] = torch.randint(
+                0, 256, (len(dp), r.shape[1]), dtype=torch.uint8, generator=gen
+            ).cuda()
+    expected = [torch.stack([r[dp].cpu() for r in rows], 1) for rows in device_rows]
+    for h in host_rows:
+        h[host_pages] = 0
+    h_idx, d_idx = _token_indices(host_pages), _token_indices(device_pages).cuda()
+    arm.write_back(h_idx, d_idx)
+    for h, e, tag in zip(host_rows, expected, ("kv", "idx")):
+        assert torch.equal(h[host_pages], e), f"{arm.name}: {tag} write-back mismatch"
+    for rows in device_rows:
+        for r in rows:
+            r[dp] = 0
+    arm.load(h_idx, d_idx)
+    for rows, e, tag in zip(device_rows, expected, ("kv", "idx")):
+        got = torch.stack([r[dp].cpu() for r in rows], 1)
+        assert torch.equal(got, e), f"{arm.name}: {tag} load mismatch"
+
+
+def _chain(
+    arm: Arm, case: str, host_pages, device_pages, pin: bool, l2_flush, steps: int
+):
+    """Median per-step load (and write-back, for `evict`) over a chain of node steps."""
+    loads, writes = [], []
+    for k in range(steps + 1):  # step 0 warms caches and allocators
+        h = _token_indices(host_pages[0 if case == "warm" else k])
+        h = h.pin_memory() if pin else h
+        d = _token_indices(device_pages[k % len(device_pages)]).cuda()
+        if case != "warm":
+            l2_flush.zero_()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        w = arm.write_back(h, d) if case == "evict" else None
+        step = arm.load(h, d)
+        if k:
+            loads.append(step)
+            if w is not None:
+                writes.append(w)
+
+    def median(xs):
+        if not xs:
+            return None
+        return Step(
+            *(statistics.median(getattr(x, f) for x in xs) for f in Step._fields)
+        )
+
+    return median(loads), median(writes)
+
+
+def _environment(pools: Pools) -> dict:
+    """What the numbers depend on beyond the arms: runtime path and NUMA placement."""
+    driver = ctypes.c_int()
+    ctypes.CDLL("libcuda.so.1").cuDriverGetVersion(ctypes.byref(driver))
+    props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)
+    return {
+        "gpu": props.name,
+        "sms": props.multi_processor_count,
+        "torch": torch.__version__,
+        "torch_cuda": torch.version.cuda,
+        "driver": driver.value,
+        # The `direct` arm batches only when dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT) finds this (transfer.cu).
+        "cudaMemcpyBatchAsync_symbol": hasattr(
+            ctypes.CDLL(None), "cudaMemcpyBatchAsync"
+        ),
+        "host_link_coherent": page_row_host_link_coherent(torch.cuda.current_device()),
+        "machine": platform.machine(),
+        "gpu_numa_node": _gpu_numa_node(f"GPU-{props.uuid}"),
+        "host_pool_numa": _numa_of(pools.kv.kv_buffer.data_ptr()),
+        "numactl_show": _cmd(["numactl", "--show"]),
+    }
+
+
+def _gpu_numa_node(gpu_id):
+    bus = _cmd(
+        ["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=pci.bus_id", "--format=csv,noheader", "-i", gpu_id]
+    )
+    if not bus:
+        return None
+    # nvidia-smi prints an 8-digit PCI domain; sysfs uses 4.
+    domain, rest = bus.strip().lower().split(":", 1)
+    try:
+        with open(f"/sys/bus/pci/devices/{domain[-4:]}:{rest}/numa_node") as f:
+            return int(f.read())
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+
+
+def _numa_of(address: int):
+    """Per-node page counts of the mapping that holds `address`, from numa_maps."""
+    try:
+        with open("/proc/self/numa_maps") as f:
+            lines = f.readlines()
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    best = None
+    for line in lines:
+        start = int(line.split()[0], 16)
+        if start <= address and (best is None or start > best[0]):
+            best = (start, line)
+    if best is None:
+        return None
+    words = (w.split("=") for w in best[1].split()[1:] if "=" in w)
+    return {k: v for k, v in words if k.startswith("N")}
+
+
+def _cmd(argv):
+    try:
+        return subprocess.run(
+            argv, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10
+        ).stdout.strip()
+    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
+        return None
+
+
+def _append(path, record):
+    if path:
+        with open(path, "a") as f:
+            f.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
+
+
+def _arms(pfd: Pools, pf, tma_quotas) -> list:
+    """(TMA quota or None, Arm) pairs."""
+    out = [
+        (None, _engine_arm(pfd, "direct", "direct")),
+        (None, _engine_arm(pfd, "direct_kernel", "direct_kernel")),
+        (None, _all_layer_arm(pfd)),
+    ]
+    if pf is not None:
+        staged = pf.kv.can_use_write_back_jit
+        out += [
+            (q, _engine_arm(pf, "kernel", f"kernel/q{q}", staged_write_cpu=staged))
+            for q in tma_quotas
+        ]
+    return out

+
+Device layers are separate allocations reached through a pointer table, and the
+host pool is a cudaHostRegister-ed [page, layer, page_bytes] buffer, as in

+Every case compares whole buffers, so it also checks that bytes outside the

+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.hicache_direct import (
+    make_hicache_direct_tables,
+    transfer_hicache_direct,
+)

+    HostTensorAllocator,
+    _cuda_host_unregister,
+    alloc_with_host_register,
+)

+

+    not torch.cuda.is_available() or not is_cuda(),
+    reason="HiCache direct_kernel transfers are CUDA-only.",
+)
+
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+PAGE_SIZE = 64
+# GLM-5.2 fp8 MLA KV page (raw 576 B rows) and DSA indexer page (128 B key + 4 B scale).
+KV_PAGE_BYTES = PAGE_SIZE * 576
+INDEXER_PAGE_BYTES = PAGE_SIZE * 132

+# layer (21), and DEP4 with the packed MTP layer (79).
+LAYER_COUNTS = [19, 21, 79]

+def _registered_host(num_pages: int, num_layers: int, page_bytes: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    host = alloc_with_host_register(
+        (num_pages, num_layers, page_bytes),
+        dtype=torch.uint8,
+        device="cpu",
+        pin_memory=True,
+        allocator=HostTensorAllocator(),
+    )
+    host.copy_(torch.randint(0, 256, host.shape, dtype=torch.uint8))
+    return host
+
+
+def _token_indices(pages: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    offsets = torch.arange(PAGE_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=pages.device)
+    return (pages[:, None] * PAGE_SIZE + offsets).reshape(-1)

+    def __init__(self, *, num_layers, num_pages, page_bytes, seed):
+        gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+        num_device_pages = 2 * num_pages + 3
+        num_host_pages = 2 * num_pages + 5
+        # Separate allocations, like the per-layer device KV and indexer buffers.
+        self.device_layers = [
+            torch.randint(0, 256, (num_device_pages, page_bytes), dtype=torch.uint8).to(
+                DEVICE
+            )
+            for _ in range(num_layers)
+        ]
+        layer_ptrs = torch.tensor(
+            [t.data_ptr() for t in self.device_layers],
+            dtype=torch.uint64,
+            device=DEVICE,
+        )
+        self.host = _registered_host(num_host_pages, num_layers, page_bytes)
+        self.tables = make_hicache_direct_tables(self.host, layer_ptrs)
+        # Device page 0 is the padding page.
+        self.device_pages = (
+            torch.randperm(num_device_pages - 1, generator=gen)[:num_pages] + 1
+        )
+        self.host_pages = torch.randperm(num_host_pages, generator=gen)[:num_pages]
+        self.device_indices = _token_indices(self.device_pages).to(DEVICE)
+        self.host_indices = _token_indices(self.host_pages).to(DEVICE)
+
+    def transfer(self, tables, *, load):
+        transfer_hicache_direct(
+            tables,
+            self.host_indices,
+            self.device_indices,
+            page_size=PAGE_SIZE,
+            load=load,
+        )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    def release(self):
+        _cuda_host_unregister(self.host)
+

+

+        pools = _Pools(**kwargs)
+        created.append(pools)
+        return pools
+

+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    for pools in created:

+    pools = make_pools(

+        num_pages=num_pages,

+        seed=num_layers,
+    )
+    expected = pools.host.clone()

+            pools.device_pages.to(DEVICE)
+        ].cpu()

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_layers", LAYER_COUNTS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_pages", [1, 17])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("page_bytes", [KV_PAGE_BYTES, INDEXER_PAGE_BYTES])

+        num_layers=num_layers,
+        num_pages=num_pages,
+        page_bytes=page_bytes,
+        seed=num_layers,
+    )

+        pools.transfer(layer_tables[layer], load=True)

+

+# 128 B lines, so they exercise the ragged segment split.
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("page_bytes", [PAGE_SIZE * 656, PAGE_SIZE * 528])
+def test_other_page_sizes_round_trip(make_pools, page_bytes):
+    pools = make_pools(num_layers=3, num_pages=5, page_bytes=page_bytes, seed=0)
+    originals = [layer.clone() for layer in pools.device_layers]
+    pools.transfer(pools.tables, load=False)

+        layer.zero_()
+    pools.transfer(pools.tables, load=True)
+    device_pages = pools.device_pages.to(DEVICE)
+    for layer, original in zip(pools.device_layers, originals):

+
+
+def test_rejects_partial_pages(make_pools):
+    """Indices that are not whole pages must not be copied."""

+            pools.device_indices[:-1],
+            page_size=PAGE_SIZE,
+            load=False,
+        )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(pools.host, snapshot)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
